eyebrow: The problem: two perimeters pretending to be one
code:
# Entra ID governs Azure access
# a SEPARATE set of AWS IAM users/keys governs AWS
#   -> created independently, no link to Entra ID
#
# user is disabled in Entra ID instantly...
# ...but their AWS access keys still work for weeks
caption: Identity silos per cloud mean disabling one account doesn't disable the other.

eyebrow: Fix: Entra ID federates into AWS

steps.label: AWS IAM Identity Center federates to Entra ID via SAML
steps.sub: no separate AWS username/password at all

steps.label: Mapped to permission sets per AWS account
steps.sub: what the federated identity is allowed to do

steps.label: Same Conditional Access policy applies
steps.sub: device compliance, risk, and CAE all still apply on this path

eyebrow: PIM and AWS STS: same idea, two clouds
code:
# Azure PIM:
#   eligible -> activate (justify, MFA, maybe approval) -> time-boxed
#
# AWS STS (via assumed role):
#   assume role -> temporary credentials -> fixed expiry
#
# both: privilege is BORROWED for a bounded window, not held
caption: Different cloud, same philosophy: time-boxed, justified, re-verified elevation.

code:
# Entra ID        = single identity source of truth
# Conditional Access = policy decision point for every sign-in
#                      (Microsoft 365, Azure, AND federated AWS)
# CAE             = keeps that decision fresh mid-session
# PIM             = time-boxed elevation in Azure
# AWS STS roles   = time-boxed elevation in AWS
caption: One identity, evaluated continuously, feeding every downstream authorization system.

subtitle: Chapter 3 moves from verifying identity to limiting what it can reach.
